### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **26** documentable anchor(s).

**32** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0c7869c03c9c6ff3a38bd6b09206edeee0184769`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **174** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0c7869c03c9c6ff3a38bd6b09206edeee0184769` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `31e8a72c573d768c1134dadcdda1f2b0268305c7` — the merge of head `2396f22385313a8a89251771061567b68d7109a5` into base `0c7869c03c9c6ff3a38bd6b09206edeee0184769`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 31e8a72c573d768c1134dadcdda1f2b0268305c7 && git checkout 31e8a72c573d768c1134dadcdda1f2b0268305c7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0c7869c03c9c6ff3a38bd6b09206edeee0184769 2396f22385313a8a89251771061567b68d7109a5 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0c7869c03c9c6ff3a38bd6b09206edeee0184769 && git merge --no-ff 2396f22385313a8a89251771061567b68d7109a5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0c7869c03c9c6ff3a38bd6b09206edeee0184769
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0c7869c03c9c6ff3a38bd6b09206edeee0184769` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

Ruling 6902014292 (option B) read against the whole package-less save address in `saveMetaItemUnaudited`, not only the hunk. The decision table, by code read:

| Case (package-less publish-mode save of `NAME`) | Before | At this head | Ruling | Pinned |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| one writable holder on A, body on A | into the holder | unchanged | unchanged | unit CONTROL, dogfood CONTROL |
| one writable holder on A, body on B | into the holder, its action moved | environment row on B | as ruled | unit, dogfood |
| one writable holder on A, object-less body | same move | environment object-less row | D4 key, consistent | unit |
| two holders on two other objects, body on B | 409 | environment row on B | D4 key; declared | unit only |
| holder on A and holder on B, both enabled, body on B | 409 | unchanged | kept as CONTROL by the area | unit CONTROL |
| managed code package ships the name | 403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE | unchanged (refused above the address, by name) | kept as CONTROL by the area | unit CONTROL, dogfood CONTROL |
| no stored row holds the name | environment row | unchanged (`candidates.length === 0` returns before any read) | unchanged | existing pins |
| any type other than `action` | generic re-address | unchanged (`type !== 'action'` returns first) | unchanged | the L234 describe, untouched |
| save naming a package, `source` set, `package-duplicate` | not asked | unchanged (outer guard untouched) | unchanged | existing pins |
| draft save (`mode=draft`) of the same body on B | inherits the holder; publish moves its action | unchanged | the ruled defect by another door | none — M1 |
| sole holder on A is disabled, body on B | into the disabled holder | environment row on B | consistent with the key | none, undeclared — S2 |
| sole binding on A is to a package that is not installed, body on B | refused 422 | environment row on B | consistent with the key | none, undeclared — S2 |
| enabled holder on A, disabled holder on B, body on B | into the enabled holder, its action moved to B | unchanged | the ruled defect, silent | none, undeclared — S3 |

- The branch fires only when `actionHeldOnlyOnOtherObjects` is true, and it is false for every non-action type, for a name no stored row binds, and as soon as one bound row sits on the saved body's object. The unchanged rows above are unchanged because `served` and the `else` arm run exactly as on main when the helper is false. Holds.
- The helper filters the item's active rows by `boundObjectOf` (the store's own owner-key reader, `objectName` then `object`, object-less sentinels folded) and re-reads the address over the remainder with no member; `action` carries no item discriminator, so the member-less read equals the door's. A stored body that does not parse keeps its holder. A failed row read rethrows unless the store is unprovisioned. Holds.
- Receipt: with `packageId` left empty the message is `Saved action 'NAME' (env-wide, state=active) [seq=N]`, pinned by exact equality in the unit test and by `not.toContain('package=')` over HTTP. It names the environment, not the package. Holds.
- Reads after the write, with the holder's row on A and the environment's row on B both stored:
  - a read naming the holder serves the holder's item on A (pinned, unit and dogfood); the action route keys by object, `/actions/A/NAME`, `/actions/B/NAME` and `/actions/_env/B/NAME` each judge the right declaration (pinned, dogfood);
  - a second package-less save on B edits the environment's row (pinned); a package-less save on A is still the holder's customization with the environment's row present (pinned, seeded);
  - the bare by-name read and the list serve the holder's item, and the environment's row has no by-name read; the PR body states it, the changeset does not (M3), and nothing pins it (N1);
  - a package-less delete of `NAME` takes the one package binding as its address whatever unbound row is stored beside it (`protocol-diff-delete-load.ts`, the delete address), so it removes the holder's row on A and leaves the environment's row. Not stated anywhere in the PR, not pinned, not routed (S1, M3).
- The dogfood file runs against what it claims: a real showcase boot, a package created over HTTP, the measured cell with the FROM answer quoted, the same-object CONTROL and the managed CONTROL on a real shipped action. CI ran it green on this head (Dogfood Regression Gate). The 409-to-row change and the object-less row are pinned at the unit level only.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` at `minor`. `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: semantic` are on both carriers, line-initial, identical; a kind other than `none` takes at least `minor` on the package the diff moves, so the level matches AGENTS.md. `semantic` is the right kind: no key, value or type is added or refused, the meaning of a save naming no package changes.
- BREAKING banner present in the changeset body and `!` in the title. ADR-0087 marker present, exactly one: `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`; the reason holds (no authorable shape moves, a row an older build re-addressed stays as stored). No schema, no export, no `.d.ts` change: the helper is module-private.
- `Skills-docs: none` reason checked at this head: `git grep` over `skills/**` for the package-less address finds only the automation skill's flow rules and the platform skill's `.custom` pair for a managed base, neither of which teaches where a package-less save of a writable package's action is written. True.
- CI on `0e5faaaa`: every check-run is completed; none is queued or running. Success: Lint and Repo Gates and its split jobs, TypeScript Type Check and its split jobs, Build Core, Test Core 8/8, Test UI, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Check PR Size. Skipped by path filter or opt-in: Lint UI, Type Check UI, Build and E2E UI, Build Docs, the queue verdicts, the opt-in harnesses. Mergeable state clean.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The diff stays inside the claimed surface as first claimed. Claim amendment 6905981763 widened the surface to `sys-metadata-repository.ts` (the draft address) with one fix round before review; this head predates that round (M1).
- No `docs/adr/**` path is in the diff. The ruling's third bullet has the ADR-0150 amendment note ride the PR and the PR land as Tier H on the maintainer's own approval; the PR body tells the maintainer nothing is needed and that the seat lands it (M2).
- Authorization: the gates that judge the item rather than its row (organization scope, the sealed managed gate, the `_lock` gate) all run above the address and are untouched; the new branch can only leave `packageId` empty, which is the address every package-less save of an unheld name already takes. No rule-layer authorization change found.
- `packages/spec` prose for `SaveMetaItemRequest.packageId` still states the address rule without the action exception (N2).

### ④ Design judgment

`protocol-save.ts` holds against the ruling for the case the ruling names and for every row it leaves unchanged; the helper is small, reads the store once more only for an action a package holds, and fails closed on an unreadable row. The PR is not ready to land as the ruling's implementation, for three reasons that are about what this head leaves out and what it says, not about the hunk.

- M1 (must-fix) — The draft door still carries the ruled defect and the PR closes the card. `SysMetadataRepository.resolveWriteHead` gives a package-less draft save the one package the item's active rows are bound to, by name alone, so the same body on B saved with `mode=draft` lands in the holder and its publish moves the holder's action. The card's landing point names the draft twin, and claim amendment 6905981763 puts it in this PR under `Fixes #34059`. Land it here with its pins (draft save on B, the publish of that draft, same-object CONTROL), and turn the changeset's "a draft save still inherits the package" line.
- M2 (must-fix) — The landing clause of the ruling is not met and the body says the opposite. Ruling 6902014292 binds an ADR-0150 amendment note, a Tier H landing and the maintainer's own approval. At this head the D4 customization paragraph and R15 still read "a customization, never a second item" for exactly the row this PR writes, no card for the note is cited (a search on the card number found none), and the 维护者速读 tells the maintainer nothing is needed. Either carry the note in this PR, or cite the filed skills card by number together with the order that lets this PR land ahead of it, and correct the "需要你做的" line so it states what the ruling asks of the maintainer.
- M3 (must-fix) — The BREAKING changeset tells the consumer "Nothing to do for the environment's own actions" while the row it now writes has no by-name read, is absent from the list, and is not what a package-less delete of the name removes. The first two are in the PR's own acceptance notes; none of the three is in the changeset, which is the text that ships. State them, with the address that does reach the environment's row today and the card that closes each.
- S1 (should-fix) — Package-less delete over the state this PR now creates on its main path removes the holder's row, by code read of the delete address (one package binding wins over a stored unbound row). The ruling's "P's item on A is untouched" then lasts until the admin undoes their own save. It is the delete door's rule, outside this surface and reachable on main by the other save order, so it is not asked for here: file it or fold it into the read half (#33904), cite the number, and pin today's answer in the dogfood file as a marked FROM so the fix turns it.
- S2 (should-fix) — "Every moved answer" in the PR body and the changeset is not every one. Two more rows move by code read and are neither declared nor pinned: a sole holder that is disabled (was written into the disabled package, now the environment's row) and a sole binding to a package that is not installed (was refused 422, now the environment's row). Both follow from the D4 key; declare and pin them, or say why they are not reachable.
- S3 (should-fix) — One row of the ruled defect survives silently: an enabled holder on A beside a disabled holder on B. The helper is false (a holder binds B), the served-address step drops the disabled holder, and the save is written into the enabled holder, moving its action to B with a receipt naming it. The area's disposition of the two-holder case rests on the refusal being loud; this one is not. Pin what it answers and route it with that follow-up, or narrow the served step to the holders at the body's object.
- N1 (nit) — The dogfood file leaves the bare by-name read unpinned by comment. Pin the current answer as a marked FROM instead, so the read-half PR has a pin to turn.
- N2 (nit) — `SaveMetaItemRequest.packageId`'s description in `packages/spec` (mirrored in `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx`) states the address rule without the action exception; "reported to the seat" needs a card number or the owner of the ADR note named for it.
